edition: 2013 modified standards / 2014 corrected CDE electronic edition
coverage_boundary: Only the complete printed-page-43 parent requirements 6.NS.5–8 and 6.EE.1 are included. 6.EE.2 crosses printed pages 43–44 and is explicitly deferred to a separate complete-parent source slice; p44–45 and later Grade 6 standards remain partial.

parent_stems.6.NS.6: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line and extend diagrams and coordinate axes to negative coordinates.
parent_stems.6.NS.7: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

source_cautions: Parent identifiers are counted once per full requirement; nested lettered subparts are required material conditions, not duplicate independent canonical skills.
Official source verified visually from CDE PDF page 49 (zero-based), corresponding to printed page 43.
No source-fidelity acceptance or canonical assessment/mastery promotion follows from the author transcription.

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Interpret positive and negative numbers as quantities of opposite directions or values in real-world settings, and explain what zero represents in each context.
required_material_conditions: positive and negative quantities in real-world contexts

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Represent rational numbers as points on number lines and coordinate planes, including negative coordinates; (a) interpret opposite signs, double negation and zero as its own opposite; (b) interpret signs in ordered pairs as quadrant locations and sign changes as reflections across axes; (c) locate rational numbers on horizontal/vertical number lines and coordinate planes.
required_material_conditions: opposite of opposite equals original and zero is its own opposite
reflections across one or both axes

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Reason about ordering and absolute value of rational numbers: (a) inequalities express relative number-line position; (b) write, interpret and explain ordering in real-world settings; (c) interpret absolute value as distance from zero and as the size of a signed quantity; (d) distinguish comparisons of magnitude from statements about signed order.
required_material_conditions: required subparts a b c d
absolute value as distance from zero
absolute value as magnitude of signed quantity
magnitude comparison not conflated with order

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Solve mathematical and real-world coordinate problems by graphing points in all four quadrants and use coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points sharing one coordinate.
required_material_conditions: distance between points with equal first coordinate or equal second coordinate
coordinate use and absolute value for axis-aligned distance

rows.author_mathematical_scope: Write and evaluate numerical expressions containing whole-number exponents.
